assessment.nobel_worthiness: Incretin physiology, from proglucagon-derived GLP-1 biology through stable analogues, has produced transformative therapies for type 2 diabetes and obesity with large, durable clinical and physiological impact. The discovery chain is clear and the importance is exceptional.
assessment.attribution: Drucker (GLP-1 actions and biology), Holst (physiology of GLP-1 secretion and effects) and Mojsov (peptide identification and synthesis) are plausible core contributors. The list also credits Lotte Bjerre Knudsen for drug development; inclusion of the translational side versus the basic side is an unresolved allocation, and the three-person cap forces exclusions.
assessment.maturity: Extensive independent confirmation across basic physiology, large randomized outcome trials and real-world use. Recognition is timely, with clinical impact now undeniable.
uncertainties: Credit allocation among basic discoverers (Habener-type contributions are not on the supplied list) and drug developers is contested.
I have not independently verified the details of priority disputes, such as Mojsov's role.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Genetically targeted light control of neural activity is a methodological revolution that enabled causal circuit dissection across neuroscience and is used in thousands of studies. It is original, clear and widely adopted as a tool.
assessment.attribution: Channelrhodopsin discovery and characterization (Nagel, Hegemann, Bamberg) and its deployment in neurons (Boyden, Deisseroth, Miesenböck) are separable contributions. Six credited names exceed the three-laureate limit, so a fair configuration is hard; I propose Deisseroth, Hegemann and Nagel, leaving Bamberg, Boyden and Miesenböck out, which is a contentious choice.
assessment.maturity: Very mature and broadly confirmed. Timing is appropriate, though translational medical outcomes (for example vision restoration) are still early, which bears on the Physiology or Medicine framing.
uncertainties: Whether a tool-based discovery best fits the Physiology or Medicine mandate versus a more direct disease link.
Attribution is fundamentally constrained by the number of credited contributors.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Engineered T cells with chimeric antigen receptors cured otherwise refractory leukemias and lymphomas, establishing a new class of living drugs. The clinical and conceptual impact is major and demonstrated.
assessment.attribution: Sadelain (CAR design and costimulation concepts), June (clinical translation and persistence in CLL and ALL) and Rosenberg (adoptive cell therapy and early gene-engineered T cells) are a coherent trio. Other foundational contributors, such as Eshhar's original chimeric receptors, are not on the supplied list, so credit is incomplete.
assessment.maturity: Multiple approved products, independent confirmations and long follow-up. Timely, though durability in solid tumors remains limited.
uncertainties: Foundational concept contributors absent from the credited names.
Safety burden and limited solid-tumor efficacy do not diminish the leukemia result but affect breadth.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: The cGAS-STING pathway defines how cytosolic DNA triggers innate immunity, connecting infection, autoimmunity, interferonopathies and anti-tumor immunity. The mechanistic clarity is strong and the conceptual impact lasting.
assessment.attribution: Chen identified cGAS and cGAMP as the second messenger, and Barber identified STING. Ishikawa, Wu and Sun made contributing discoveries but a two-person core is supportable from the supplied credit.
assessment.maturity: Well confirmed with structural and genetic work across labs. Therapeutic translation is still maturing, so recognition could be seen as somewhat early.
uncertainties: Clinical validation of STING-targeted therapies is incomplete.
Relative weighting of Barber versus Ishikawa and the other STING contributors.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Splice-modulating antisense oligonucleotide therapy for SMN2 showed that RNA processing can be corrected pharmacologically, leading to nusinersen and a dramatic change in the course of spinal muscular atrophy. The work links RNA splicing mechanism to cure-level clinical impact.
assessment.attribution: Krainer defined the splicing mechanism and identified the targetable sequence, and Bennett led antisense chemistry and development. This is a clean two-person configuration. Contributions by Hua and others could be raised and are not in the list.
assessment.maturity: Approved therapy with years of clinical follow-up and confirmation. Timing is reasonable.
uncertainties: Prior recognition of antisense chemistry pioneers may complicate the framing of the prize.
Detail of contributions of other developers is not verified.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Establishing adult stem-cell-derived organoids opened a general platform for modelling tissue homeostasis, cancer and infection, and for personalized medicine. Originality is high and the method is widely adopted.
assessment.attribution: Clevers led the Lgr5 stem-cell and organoid culture work with Sato as first author on the key intestinal organoid paper; the two-person credit is clean. Other organoid pioneers (e.g., Sasai-type pluripotent organoids) are outside this candidate's scope.
assessment.maturity: Broadly reproduced and growing clinical uses, but therapeutic outcomes remain emerging, so impact is partly prospective.
uncertainties: Whether the prize would be seen as a technology rather than a discovery prize.
Overlap with the Lgr5 stem-cell discovery and with pluripotent-derived organoids.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Imatinib and BCR-ABL-directed therapy turned chronic myeloid leukemia into a manageable disease and established the paradigm of molecularly targeted cancer treatment. The clinical result is among the clearest in modern oncology.
assessment.attribution: Druker (clinical development), Lydon (compound discovery and project origin) and Sawyers (resistance mechanisms and next-generation inhibitors) form a natural trio. Contributions of Rowley and Nowell (chromosome) and Witte, Baltimore and Wang (BCR-ABL kinase biology) are outside this list, so credit may be perceived as incomplete.
assessment.maturity: Over two decades of confirmation and survival data, so very mature; arguably overdue, but the Lasker precedent suggests recognition may be considered already substantial.
uncertainties: Upstream basic discoveries leading to BCR-ABL are not credited here.
Possible view that pharmaceutical development has been honored by other prizes.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Discovery of TOR as the target of rapamycin and its role in growth control and nutrient signalling is a foundational insight into cell growth, metabolism, aging and cancer, with clinical relevance for immunosuppression and oncology.
assessment.attribution: Hall identified TOR genetically and defined its function; Schreiber contributed through the chemical biology of rapamycin and FKBP12 and the identification of mammalian targets. Sabatini's contributions on mTORC1 regulation are credited but I leave him out given allocation limits and uncertainty, which I have not independently verified.
assessment.maturity: Strong confirmation in many systems over decades. Recognition is timely and likely to be seen as important.
uncertainties: Contributions of Heitman, Hall and Sabatini-lab work on pathway components, plus the Schreiber role, make attribution contestable.
I am relying on memory for priority details.
